newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends flat on likely intervention.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends flat on likely intervention.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed virtually unchanged against the U.S. dollar on Friday on what dealers called likely central bank intervention as the easing currency dipped toward T$28 in late-day trade.
The dollar fell as low as T$27.913 but recovered near the close to finish at T$27.867 against Thursday's T$27.869 close.
Turnover was a heavy US$397.5 million.
Dealers said the central bank entered in afternoon trade.
"Apparently, the central bank wants to tell the market the Taiwan dollar should not fall so much so quick," said one dealer.
Dealers said central bank intervention, which is seldom acknowledged publicly, also was apparent on Wednesday and Thursday.
They said Taiwan dollar depreciation pressure remained heavy as foreign funds continued to pull out profits taken in the consolidating stock market.
Trade demands also pushed the Taiwan dollar softer, further fuelling speculation that the dollar was depreciating.
"Importers had strong U.S. dollar demand today. Plus, of course, there is certain speculation as many expect the Taiwan dollar to fall further," the dealer said.

Senior Taipei dealers said in an informal Reuters Poll on Friday that Taiwan's easing dollar was likely to break eight-year support at T$28 in the third quarter, citing slack economic growth and political uncertainties.
But they cautioned that the central bank was determined to defend the Taiwan dollar's stability to prevent an acceleration of capital outflows that would hurt Taiwan people's confidence.

The Taipei trading rooms chiefs at six prominent local and international banks gave their forecasts for the Taiwan dollar on the condition of anonymity, citing the acute sensitivities about currency movements in Taiwan.

Four out of six senior dealers polled by Reuters said the Taiwan dollar would break T$28 for a short period of time, but that central bank intervention could be expected to pull the local dollar back to consolidate in a T$27.80-28.00 range.
Two of the dealers said the central bank would mount such a strenuous defence that the dollar would not breach T$28.
For Saturday, a T$27.85-27.90 range was seen.
